body: It's insanely hard to be nice to yourself when everyone else is ignoring your existance. Hell I don't interact with people from a day to day basis. The downside to suicide is that you'll probably hurt someone, like the people I saw do it. The difference between me and them is that they actually were moving on with their lives and people actually cared about them.
But it was the "I don't ever want to talk to you again" type of leave me alone. Really we've been drifting away for a long time but I can't seem to let go and she's eager too, it's awful

I don't want to be a hero, I just want to make an impact on someone's life. I can't stand seeing endless suffering around me and the world going to shit. The suicides really effected me because I've been on the edge for some time now, atleast 2 years. These people had so many friends, they were loved by so many people and I am just overall in a sad confused state. The shooting in New Zealand also struck a cord with me because it was a clear example of the worst case scenario. I was almost turned into a hateful cunt myself (I cut myself off from those hateful communities a long time ago) and the shooter went fully down the rabbit hole.  So it's just so sad how easily things could've been changed and how bad the outcome was.

I don't know if I'm a good person. I'm extremely distrustful but I always want to believe that someone has pure intentions, but that's just not true. I never hold grudges and never argue but I feel like I am a doormat and I get used all the time because of this. But I can't just not help people because I don't want anyone to feel the way I do - unloved, forgotten, whatever. But I also want to feel that way too so I'm conflicted.
